parameter.definition: A data item involved in PBPK modelling.

physiologically based pharmacokinetic mo.definition: A data representation model that predicts the absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) of chemical substances in biological species based on physiological principles using mathematical modelling technique.

whole body pbpk.definition: A physiologically based pharmacokinetic model that contains an explicit representation of the organs most relevant to the ADME of the compound.

perfusion limited model.definition: A physiologically based pharmacokinetic model that assumes tissue concentration reaches equilibrium rapidly and uptake/elimination is limited by blood flow rate.

physiological parameter.definition: A parameter that provides the structural framework for a PBPK model and relates to the organism's physiology (e.g., body weight, organ volume, blood flow).

body mass index.definition: A physiological parameter calculated as an individual's weight (kg) divided by the square of their height (m).

bodyweight.definition: A physiological parameter representing the mass or quantity of heaviness of an individual.

height.definition: A physiological parameter describing the distance from the bottom to the top of someone standing upright.

surface area.definition: A physiological parameter representing the total area that the surface of an object occupies.

assigned race.definition: A parameter representing a geographic ancestral origin category assigned to a population group.

blood flow rate to compartment.definition: A bodily fluid flow rate parameter representing the rate of blood flow in different parts of the body

cardiac output rate.definition: A blood flow rate parameter representing the volume of blood pumped by the heart compartment per unit of time.

blood flow rate to stomach.definition: A blood flow rate parameter specifically describing the rate to the stomach compartment.

fraction of blood flow to stomach.definition: The dimensionless fraction of cardiac output delivered to the stomach compartment.

blood flow rate to intestine.definition: A blood flow parameter specifically describing the rate to the intestine compartment.

fraction of blood flow to intestine.definition: The dimensionless fraction of cardiac output delivered to the intestine compartment.

blood flow rate to small intestine.definition: A blood flow rate parameter specifically describing the rate to the small intestine compartment.

fraction of blood flow to small intestin.definition: The dimensionless fraction of cardiac output delivered to the small intestine compartment.

blood flow rate to large intestine.definition: A blood flow rate parameter specifically describing the rate to the large intestine compartment.

fraction of blood flow to large intestin.definition: The dimensionless fraction of cardiac output delivered to the large intestine compartment.

blood flow rate to pancreas.definition: A blood flow rate parameter specifically describing the rate to the pancreas compartment.

fraction of blood flow to pancreas.definition: The dimensionless fraction of cardiac output delivered to the pancreas compartment.

blood flow rate to liver.definition: A blood flow rate parameter specifically describing the rate to the liver compartment.

fraction of blood flow to liver.definition: The dimensionless fraction of cardiac output delivered to the liver compartment.

blood flow rate to kidney.definition: A blood flow rate parameter specifically describing the rate to the kidney compartment.

fraction of blood flow to kidney.definition: The dimensionless fraction of cardiac output delivered to the kidney compartment.

blood flow rate to muscle.definition: A blood flow rate parameter specifically describing the rate to the muscle compartment.

fraction of blood flow to muscle.definition: The dimensionless fraction of cardiac output delivered to the muscle compartment.

blood flow rate to heart.definition: A blood flow rate parameter specifically describing the rate to the heart compartment.

fraction of blood flow to heart.definition: The dimensionless fraction of cardiac output delivered to the heart compartment.

blood flow rate to fat.definition: A blood flow rate parameter specifically describing the rate to the fat (adipose tissue) compartment.

fraction of blood flow to fat.definition: The dimensionless fraction of cardiac output delivered to the fat compartment.

blood flow rate to gonad.definition: A blood flow parameter specifically describing the rate to the gonads compartment.

fraction of blood flow to gonad.definition: The dimensionless fraction of cardiac output delivered to the gonad compartment.

blood flow rate to skin.definition: A blood flow rate parameter specifically describing the rate to the skin compartment.

fraction of blood flow to skin.definition: The dimensionless fraction of cardiac output delivered to the skin compartment.

blood flow rate to bone.definition: A blood flow rate parameter specifically describing the rate to the bone compartment.

fraction of blood flow to bone.definition: The dimensionless fraction of cardiac output delivered to the bone compartment.

blood flow rate to brain.definition: A blood flow rate parameter specifically describing the rate to the brain compartment.

fraction of blood flow to brain.definition: The dimensionless fraction of cardiac output delivered to the brain compartment.

blood flow rate to spleen.definition: A blood flow rate parameter specifically describing the rate to the spleen compartment.

fraction of blood flow to spleen.definition: The dimensionless fraction of cardiac output delivered to the spleen compartment.

blood flow rate to lung.definition: A blood flow rate parameter specifically describing the rate to the lung compartment.

fraction of blood flow to lung.definition: The dimensionless fraction of cardiac output delivered to the lung compartment.

blood flow rate to poorly perfused.definition: A blood flow rate parameter specifically describing the rate to the poorly perfused organ/tissue compartment.

fraction of blood flow to poorly perfuse.definition: The dimensionless fraction of cardiac output delivered to the poorly perfused compartment.

blood flow rate to richly perfused.definition: A blood flow rate parameter specifically describing the rate to the richly perfused organ/tissue compartment.

fraction of blood flow to richly perfuse.definition: The dimensionless fraction of cardiac output delivered to the richly perfused compartment.

blood flow rate to restbody.definition: A blood flow rate parameter specifically describing the rate to the rest of body compartment (total minus specified organs).

fraction of blood flow to restbody.definition: The dimensionless fraction of cardiac output delivered to the rest of the body compartment.

blood flow rate to gall bladder.definition: A blood flow rate parameter specifically describing the rate to the gall bladder compartment.

fraction of blood flow to gall bladder.definition: The dimensionless fraction of cardiac output delivered to the gall bladder compartment.

blood flow rate to portal vein.definition: A blood flow rate parameter specifically describing the rate to the portal vein compartment.

fraction of blood flow to portal vein.definition: The dimensionless fraction of cardiac output delivered to the portal vein compartment.

blood flow rate to lymph.definition: A blood flow rate parameter specifically describing the rate to the lymph compartment.

fraction of blood flow to lymph.definition: The dimensionless fraction of cardiac output delivered to the lymph compartment.

amount of metabolized.definition: An output parameter representing the total amount of compound metabolized.

fraction of blood flow to stratum corneu.definition: The dimensionless fraction of cardiac output delivered to the stratum corneum compartment.

fraction of exposed skin.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the exposed skin volume divided per unit of total body weight.

fraction of unexposed skin.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the unexposed skin volume divided per unit of total body weight.

arterial blood flow rate.definition: A blood flow rate parameter representing the rate of blood flow through the arterial compartment.

venous blood flow rate.definition: A blood flow rate parameter representing the rate of blood flow returning through the venous compartment.

glomerular filtration rate.definition: A bodily fluid flow rate parameter (or physiological process measure) describing the flow rate of filtered fluid through the kidney compartment.

volume of compartment.definition: A physiological parameter representing the volume of a specific organ or tissue.

volume of stomach.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the stomach compartment.

fraction of stomach.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the stomach volume divided per unit of total body weight.

volume of intestine.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the intestine compartment.

fraction of intestine.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the intestine volume divided per unit of total body weight.

volume of small intestine.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the small intestine compartment.

fraction of small intestine.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the small intestine volume divided per unit of total body weight.

volume of large intestine.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the large intestine compartment.

fraction of large intestine.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the large intestine volume divided per unit of total body weight.

volume of pancreas.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the pancreas compartment.

fraction of pancreas.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the pancreas volume divided per unit of total body weight.

volume of liver.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the liver compartment.

fraction of liver.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the liver volume divided per unit of total body weight.

volume of kidney.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the kidney compartment.

fraction of kidney.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the kidney volume divided per unit of total body weight.

volume of muscle.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of muscle compartment.

fraction of muscle.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the muscle volume divided per unit of total body weight.

volume of heart.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the heart compartment.

fraction of heart.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the heart volume divided per unit of total body weight.

volume of fat.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of fat (adipose tissue) compartment.

fraction of fat.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the fat volume divided per unit of total body weight.

volume of gonad.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the gonad compartment.

fraction of gonad.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the gonad volume divided per unit of total body weight.

volume of skin.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the skin compartment.

fraction of skin.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the skin volume divided per unit of total body weight.

volume of bone.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of bone compartment.

fraction of bone.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the bone volume divided per unit of total body weight.

volume of brain.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the brain compartment.

fraction of brain.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the brain volume divided per unit of total body weight.

volume of spleen.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the spleen compartment.

fraction of spleen.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the spleen volume divided per unit of total body weight.

volume of lung.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the lung compartment.

fraction of lung.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the lung volume divided per unit of total body weight.

volume of poorly perfused.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the poorly perfused compartment.

fraction of poorly perfused.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the poorly perfused compartment volume divided per unit of total body weight.

volume of richly perfused.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the richly perfused compartment.

fraction of richly perfused.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the richly perfused compartment volume divided per unit of total body weight.

volume of plasma.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of plasma compartment.

fraction of plasma.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the plasma volume divided per unit of total body weight.

volume of rest body.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the rest of body compartment.

fraction of rest body.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the rest of body volume divided per unit of total body weight.

volume of stratum corneum with respect t.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of stratum corneum compartment with respect to blood/plasma.

volume of blood.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of blood compartment.

volume of exposed skin.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the exposed skin compartment.

fraction of surface area exposed.definition: A surface area parameter representing the fraction of skin surface area actually exposed.

volume of unexposed skin.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the unexposed skin compartment.

volume of stratum corneum exposed.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the exposed stratum corneum compartment.

volume of unexposed stratum corneum.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the unexposed stratum corneum compartment.

fraction alveolar volume.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the alveolar volume divided per unit of total body weight.

volume of gall bladder.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the gall bladder compartment.

fraction of gall bladder.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the gall bladder volume divided per unit of total body weight.

volume of portal vein.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the portal vein compartment.

fraction of portal vein.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the portal vein volume divided per unit of total body weight.

volume of lymph.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of lymph compartment.

fraction of lymph.definition: A dimensionless fraction of volume defined as the lymph volume divided per unit of total body weight.

arterial volume.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the arterial compartment.

venous volume.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the venous compartment.

physicochemical parameter.definition: A parameter relating to the physical and chemical properties of a compound (e.g., MW, lipophilicity, solubility, pKa).

molecular weight.definition: A physicochemical parameter representing the sum of the weights of all atoms in a molecule.

lipophillicity.definition: A physicochemical parameter representing the affinity or tendency of a compound to dissolve in lipids or hydrophobic environments.

distribution coefficient.definition: A physicochemical parameter representing the logarithm of the ratio of concentrations of a compound in a mixture of two immiscible phases at equilibrium, specifically describing lipophilicity (LogD).

dissolution in two phase system.definition: A physicochemical parameter representing the ratio of a dissolved compound in a two-phase system (often used interchangeably with partition coefficient).

logarithmic solubility.definition: A physicochemical parameter representing the 10-based logarithm of a compound's solubility (typically in mol/L).

water solubility.definition: A physicochemical parameter representing the solubility of a compound specifically in water.

acid dissociation constant.definition: A physicochemical parameter representing the negative base-10 logarithm (pKa) of the acid dissociation constant (Ka).

basic dissociation constant.definition: A physicochemical parameter representing the negative base-10 logarithm (pKb) of the base dissociation constant (Kb).

physiological charge.definition: A physicochemical parameter representing the electrical charge of a molecule at physiological pH.

hydrogen acceptor count.definition: A physicochemical parameter representing the integer number of hydrogen bond acceptors in a molecular entity.

hydrogen donor count.definition: A physicochemical parameter representing the integer number of hydrogen bond donors in a molecular entity.

rotatable bond count.definition: A physicochemical parameter representing the integer count of rotatable bonds in a molecular entity.

biochemical parameter.definition: A parameter that is compound-dependent and relates to biological interactions or transformations (e.g., clearance, binding, partition coefficients).

absorption.definition: A biological process by which a compound moves from its site of administration into the systemic circulation or a target tissue.

absorption rate constant gut.definition: An absorption rate constant parameter representing the rate constant for the movement of a compound from the gut to systemic circulation or another compartment.

absorption rate constant intestine.definition: An absorption rate constant parameter representing the movement of a compound from the intestine to systemic circulation or another compartment.

gastric emptying rate.definition: A biochemical parameter representing the rate at which the stomach empties its contents into the small intestine.

enterohepatic recirculation.definition: A biological process involving recycling of compounds through the liver via biliary excretion, intestinal reabsorption, portal circulation return, and re-excretion.

specific intestinal permeability.definition: A biochemical parameter representing the surface area-normalized transcellular permeability of the intestinal wall for a compound.

distribution process.definition: A biological process describing the movement of a compound from systemic circulation to various organs/tissues.

volume of distribution.definition: A biochemical parameter representing the apparent volume into which a compound distributes in the body relative to its plasma concentration.

protein binding mediated distributiion p.definition: A distribution process (or molecular function) where substances bind to proteins or related compounds.

unbound fraction.definition: A biochemical parameter representing the fraction of a compound that is not bound (e.g., to proteins).

fraction unbound gut.definition: An unbound fraction parameter specifically for the gut compartment.

fraction unbound stomach.definition: An unbound fraction parameter specifically for the stomach compartment.

fraction unbound intestine.definition: An unbound fraction parameter specifically for the intestine compartment.

fraction unbound pancreas.definition: An unbound fraction parameter specifically for the pancreas compartment.

fraction unbound liver.definition: An unbound fraction parameter specifically for the liver compartment.

fraction unbound kidney.definition: An unbound fraction parameter specifically for the kidney compartment.

fraction unbound muscle.definition: An unbound fraction parameter specifically for the muscle compartment.

fraction unbound heart.definition: An unbound fraction parameter specifically for the heart compartment.

fraction unbound fat.definition: An unbound fraction parameter specifically for the fat (adipose) compartment.

fraction unbound gonad.definition: An unbound fraction parameter specifically for the gonad compartment.

fraction unbound skin.definition: An unbound fraction parameter specifically for the skin compartment.

fraction unbound bone.definition: An unbound fraction parameter specifically for the bone compartment.

fraction unbound spleen.definition: An unbound fraction parameter specifically for the spleen compartment.

fraction unbound lung.definition: An unbound fraction parameter specifically for the lung compartment.

fraction unbound enterocytes.definition: An unbound fraction parameter specifically within enterocytes.

partition coefficient.definition: A biochemical parameter representing the ratio of the concentration of a compound in a particular tissue to its concentration in plasma/blood at equilibrium.

gut plasma partition coefficient.definition: A partition coefficient representing the ratio of compound concentration in gut to plasma.

stomach plasma partition coefficient.definition: A partition coefficient representing the ratio of compound concentration in stomach to plasma.

intestine plasma partition coefficient.definition: A partition coefficient representing the ratio of compound concentration in intestine to plasma.

pancreas plasma partition coefficient.definition: A partition coefficient representing the ratio of compound concentration in pancreas to plasma.

liver plasma partition coefficient.definition: A partition coefficient representing the ratio of compound concentration in liver to plasma.

kidney plasma partition coefficient.definition: A partition coefficient representing the ratio of compound concentration in kidney to plasma.

muscle plasma partition coefficient.definition: A partition coefficient representing the ratio of compound concentration in muscle to plasma.

heart plasma partition coefficient.definition: A partition coefficient representing the ratio of compound concentration in heart to plasma.

fat plasma partition coefficient.definition: A partition coefficient representing the ratio of compound concentration in fat (adipose tissue) to plasma.

gonad plasma partition coefficient.definition: A partition coefficient representing the ratio of compound concentration in gonads to plasma.

skin plasma partition coefficient.definition: A partition coefficient representing the ratio of compound concentration in skin to plasma.

bone plasma partition coefficient.definition: A partition coefficient representing the ratio of compound concentration in bone to plasma.

spleen plasma partition coefficient.definition: A partition coefficient representing the ratio of compound concentration in spleen to plasma.

lung plasma partition coefficient.definition: A partition coefficient representing the ratio of compound concentration in lung to plasma.

rich perfused plasma partition coefficie.definition: A partition coefficient representing the ratio of compound concentration in the lumped richly perfused compartment to plasma.

poor perfused plasma partition coefficie.definition: A partition coefficient representing the ratio of compound concentration in the lumped poorly perfused compartment to plasma.

skin stratum corneum partition coefficie.definition: A partition coefficient representing the ratio of compound concentration in the stratum corneum to the rest of the skin.

air plasma partition coefficient.definition: A partition coefficient representing the ratio of compound concentration in air to plasma.

skin diffusion coefficient.definition: A diffusion coefficient representing the diffusion of a compound across the skin.

human serum albumin.definition: A material entity representing distribution-related protein (most abundant in human plasma) that binds various compounds.

blood:plasma ratio.definition: A biochemical parameter representing the ratio of compound concentration in whole blood to that in plasma.

catalytic rate constant.definition: A biochemical parameter quantifying enzymatic reaction velocity (kcat), representing the maximum number of substrate molecules converted per active site per unit time.

phase I metabolism.definition: A metabolism process involving the conversion of exogenous substances to more polar metabolites, often via oxidation, reduction, or hydrolysis (e.g., by CYPs).

phase II.definition: A metabolism process involving the conjugation of phase I products (or parent compounds) to hydrophilic moieties to facilitate excretion.

phase III.definition: A metabolism/transport process involving the further processing and excretion of conjugated metabolites (often involving efflux transporters).

first pass metabolism.definition: A metabolism process occurring at a specific location (e.g., liver, gut wall) after administration but before reaching systemic circulation, reducing the concentration of active compound.

maximum rate in intestine.definition: A maximum rate (Vmax) of an enzyme catalysed reaction for a compound in the intestine when the enzyme is saturated with substrate.

Michaelis constant intestine.definition: Michaelis constant representing the substrate concentration at which the reaction rate in the intestine is half of Vmax (Km).

maximum rate in liver.definition: A maximum rate (Vmax) of an enzyme catalysed reaction for a compound in the liver when the enzyme is saturated with substrate.

Michaelis constant liver.definition: Michaelis constant representing the substrate concentration at which the reaction rate in the liver is half of Vmax (Km).

gut metabolism.definition: A metabolism process specifically occurring within the gut.

dissociation constant.definition: A biochemical parameter (Kd) measuring the affinity of a compound for its binding partner (e.g., receptor, protein).

transporter.definition: A material entity representing protein responsible for the import or export of compounds across cell membranes.

oatp.definition: A transporter family (Organic Anion Transporting Polypeptides) involved in transporting organic anions.

abcc3.definition: A transporter (ATP-binding cassette subfamily C member 3) involved in bile metabolism and transport.

abcc2.definition: A transporter (ATP-binding cassette subfamily C member 2) involved in transporting various molecules across cell membranes.

degradation rate constant.definition: A biochemical parameter (kdeg) representing the rate constant for the degradation of a metabolizing enzyme or transporter.

inhibition constant.definition: A biochemical parameter (Ki) representing the inhibition constant for a specific enzyme or transporter interaction.

renal excretion.definition: An excretion process involving the elimination of compounds and metabolites primarily through urine via the kidneys.

hepatic excretion.definition: An excretion process involving the elimination of compounds and metabolites via the liver (often into bile).

fecal excretion.definition: An excretion process involving the elimination of compounds and metabolites through feces.

exhalation.definition: An excretion process involving the elimination of volatile compounds and metabolites through respiration.

sweat excretion.definition: An excretion process involving the elimination of compounds and metabolites through sweat.

hair excretion.definition: An excretion process involving the elimination and deposition of compounds and metabolites into hair.

clearance rate.definition: A biochemical parameter representing the volume of biological fluid cleared of a compound per unit time.

fecal clearance rate.definition: A clearance rate specifically quantifying elimination via feces.

sweat clearance rate.definition: A clearance rate specifically quantifying elimination via sweat.

urinary clearance rate.definition: A clearance rate specifically quantifying elimination via urine.

biliary clearance rate.definition: A clearance rate specifically quantifying elimination via bile.

hepatic clearance rate.definition: A clearance rate specifically quantifying elimination via the liver (metabolism and/or biliary excretion).

intrinsic clearance rate.definition: A clearance rate representing the inherent ability of an organ or tissue to eliminate a compound, independent of blood flow or binding.

fecal elimination rate constant.definition: A biochemical parameter representing the rate constant for elimination via fecal excretion.

renal elimination rate constant.definition: A biochemical parameter representing the rate constant for elimination via renal (urinary) excretion.

biliary elimination.definition: An elimination process involving the irreversible transfer of compound or metabolites from plasma to bile via hepatocytes.

route of exposure.definition: A parameter designating the body part or method through which exposure is introduced.

oral exposure.definition: A route of exposure via the mouth.

dermal exposure.definition: A route of exposure via the skin.

inhalation exposure.definition: A route of exposure via inhalation into the lungs.

intravenous bolus exposure.definition: A route of exposure involving rapid injection directly into a vein.

intravenous infusion exposure.definition: A route of exposure involving continuous administration directly into a vein over time.

intramuscular exposure.definition: A route of exposure involving injection into a muscle.

intraarterial exposure.definition: A route of exposure involving administration directly into an artery.

intrathecal exposure.definition: A route of exposure involving administration into the spinal canal.

subcutaneous exposure.definition: A route of exposure involving administration under the skin.

nasal exposure.definition: A route of exposure via the nasal passages.

transdermal exposure.definition: A route of exposure involving absorption through the skin, typically from a patch.

ocular exposure.definition: A route of exposure via the eye.

output parameter.definition: A parameter representing a result or prediction generated by the PBPK model.

peak concentration.definition: An output parameter representing the highest concentration (Cmax) of a compound achieved after exposure.

maximum steady state concentration.definition: An output parameter representing the maximum concentration (Cmax,ss) achieved at steady state during repeated dosing.

maximum time.definition: An output parameter representing the time (Tmax) required to reach the peak concentration.

area under curve.definition: An output parameter representing the integral of the concentration-time curve (AUC), indicating total exposure.

area under curve 0 to t.definition: An area under curve parameter calculated from time zero to a specific time point t (AUC0-t).

area under curve last.definition: An area under curve parameter calculated from time zero to the time of the last measurable concentration (AUClast).

area under curve 0 to infinity.definition: An area under curve parameter extrapolated from time zero to infinity (AUC0-inf), representing total exposure after a single dose.

area under moment curve.definition: An output parameter calculated as the integral of the product of time and concentration versus time (AUMC).

mean residence time.definition: An output parameter representing the average time a compound resides in the body (MRT).

half-life.definition: An output parameter representing the time required for the compound concentration to decrease by half (t1/2).

bioavailability.definition: An output parameter representing the rate and extent to which an active compound is absorbed and becomes available at the site of action or systemic circulation.

relative bioavailability.definition: A bioavailability parameter comparing the rate and extent of absorption of a test compound to a reference compound.

mean absorption time.definition: An output parameter representing the average time for a compound to be absorbed into systemic circulation (MAT).

mean dissolution time.definition: An output parameter representing the average time for a compound to dissolve in the body (MDT).

bioequivalence.definition: An output parameter indicating comparable bioavailability between test and reference formulations under similar conditions.

absolute bioavailability.definition: A bioavailability parameter comparing the amount reaching systemic circulation after non-IV administration to the amount available after IV administration.

elimination phase.definition: An elimination process phase describing the period where removal of the compound from the body predominates.

absorption phase.definition: An absorption process phase describing the period where the compound moves from the administration site into systemic circulation.

amount in urine.definition: The amount of compound in the urine compartment.

amount in feces.definition: The amount of compound in the feces compartment.

cumulative amount in urine.definition: An output parameter representing the total amount of compound excreted in urine over a specific time period.

cumulative amount in feces.definition: An output parameter representing the total amount of compound excreted in feces over a specific time period.

steady state area under curve.definition: An area under curve parameter calculated over a dosing interval at steady state (AUCss).

min organ concentration.definition: An output parameter representing the minimum concentration of a compound in a specific organ after exposure.

max organ concentration.definition: An output parameter representing the maximum concentration of a compound in a specific organ after exposure.

median organ concentration.definition: An output parameter representing the median concentration of a compound in a specific organ after exposure.

percentile 2.5 cplasma.definition: A plasma concentration parameter representing the 2.5th percentile of the plasma concentration distribution in a population simulation.

percentile 97.5 cplasma.definition: A plasma concentration parameter representing the 97.5th percentile of the plasma concentration distribution in a population simulation.

tolerable daily intake.definition: An output parameter (or exposure limit) estimating the amount of a substance that can be ingested daily over a lifetime without appreciable health risk (TDI).

reconstructed exposure.definition: An output parameter estimating the amount of compound exposure based on internal body measurements.

estimated daily intake.definition: An output parameter estimating the amount of a compound consumed daily (EDI).

biomonitoring equivalent.definition: An output parameter representing the concentration of a chemical (or metabolite) in a biological medium consistent with exposure guidance values (BE).

reference dose.definition: An output parameter (or exposure limit) estimating the daily oral or dermal exposure likely to be without appreciable risk over a lifetime (RfD).

acceptable daily intake.definition: An output parameter (or exposure limit) estimating the amount of a substance in food/water that can be consumed daily without appreciable health risk (ADI).

reference human data set.definition: A data set containing the physiological parameters representing a standard human, often defined by specific characteristics like 70 kg body weight.

biological matrix concentration.definition: An output parameter representing the total concentration of a compound in a specified biological matrix.

concentration in hair.definition: The total concentration of compound in the hair compartment.

concentration in nail.definition: A biological matrix concentration specifically representing the total concentration of compound in the nail compartment.

concentration in teeth.definition: A biological matrix concentration specifically representing the total concentration of compound in the teeth compartment.

concentration in blood.definition: The total concentration of compound in the blood compartment.

concentration in urine.definition: A biological matrix concentration specifically representing the total concentration of compound in the urine compartment.

permeability limited pbpk.definition: A physiologically based pharmacokinetic model that considers the permeability across membranes as a limiting factor for compound distribution.

maximum rate of basolateral transporter.definition: Maximum rate (Vmax) of transport via a basolateral transporter, measured in vitro.

Michaelis constant baso.definition: Michaelis constant representing the substrate concentration at half-maximal velocity (Km) for a basolateral transporter.

maximum rate of apical transporter in vi.definition: A maximum rate (Vmax) of an enzyme catalysed reaction for a compound across the apical membrane of an organ, measured in vitro, when the enzyme is saturated with substrate.

Michaelis constant apical.definition: Michaelis constant representing the substrate concentration at half-maximal velocity (Km) for an apical transporter.

influx constant.definition: A biochemical parameter (kin) describing the rate constant for compound movement into a cell or compartment.

efflux rate constant.definition: A biochemical parameter (kefflux) describing the rate constant for compound movement out of a cell or compartment.

plasma space.definition: A physiological parameter representing the volume occupied by plasma within a tissue or the body.

endosomal space compartment.definition: A compartment representing the endosomal space within cells.

interstitial space.definition: A physiological parameter representing the fluid-filled space between blood vessels and cells.

effective permeability.definition: A biochemical parameter (Peff) representing the rate at which a compound passes through a biological barrier (e.g., intestinal wall).

population pbpk.definition: A physiologically based pharmacokinetic model approach used to characterize interindividual variability within a population.

top-down pbpk.definition: A physiologically based pharmacokinetic model approach primarily based on fitting observed clinical data, often empirical.

bottom-up pbpk.definition: A physiologically based pharmacokinetic model approach built mechanistically using in vitro and physiological data.

one-compartment pbpk.definition: A physiologically based pharmacokinetic model that treats the entire body as a single, kinetically homogenous unit (central compartment).

central compartment.definition: A compartment in a multi-compartment model representing plasma and highly perfused tissues where distribution is rapid.

peripheral compartment.definition: A compartment in a multi-compartment model representing tissues where compound distribution is slower compared to the central compartment.

elimination.definition: A biological process involving the irreversible removal of a compound from the body, encompassing metabolism and excretion.

linear elimination.definition: An elimination process that follows first-order kinetics (rate proportional to concentration).

non-linear elimination.definition: An elimination process that does not follow first-order kinetics (e.g., saturable processes).

lifestage.definition: A physiological parameter representing distinct phases of an individual's life (e.g., infant, adult, geriatric).

fetus lifestage.definition: A lifestage parameter representing the unborn offspring from the postembryonic stage until birth.

infant lifestage.definition: A lifestage parameter representing a very young child, typically under one year of age.

toddler lifestage.definition: A lifestage parameter representing a young child, typically between one and three years old.

child lifestage.definition: A lifestage parameter representing individuals typically between 3 and 11 years old.

teenager lifestage.definition: A lifestage parameter representing individuals typically between eleven and fifteen years old.

adolescent lifestage.definition: A lifestage parameter representing the transitional stage between teenager and adulthood (approx. 15-18 years).

adult lifestage.definition: A lifestage parameter representing individuals typically from eighteen to thirty years old.

middle age lifestage.definition: A lifestage parameter representing individuals typically from thirty to forty-five years old.

old age lifestage.definition: A lifestage parameter representing individuals typically from forty-five to sixty years old (or older, definitions vary).

pediatric lifestage.definition: A lifestage parameter representing individuals typically below fifteen years of age.

geriatric lifestage.definition: A lifestage parameter representing older adults, often considered 60/65 years and older.

brain pbpk.definition: A physiologically based pharmacokinetic model specifically built to predict compound concentrations in the brain.

cerebrospinal fluid volume.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) compartment in the spinal region.

cranial cerebrospinal fluid volume.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) compartment in the cranial region.

brain mass.definition: A physiological parameter representing the mass of the brain.

blood brain barrier compartment.definition: A barrier compartment representing the blood-brain barrier (BBB).

spinal cerebrospinal fluid flow rate.definition: A bodily fluid flow rate parameter representing the flow rate of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) compartment in the spinal region.

cranial cerebrospinal fluid flow rate.definition: A bodily fluid flow rate parameter representing the flow rate of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) compartment in the cranial region.

blood cerebrospinal fluid compartment.definition: A barrier compartment representing the blood-cerebrospinal fluid barrier (BCSFB).

volume of hippocampus.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the hippocampus compartment.

volume of frontal cortex.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the frontal cortex compartment.

volume of cerebrum.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the cerebrum compartment.

volume of cerebellum.definition: A volume parameter representing the total volume of the cerebellum compartment.
